Hi Laura / Dan —

Thanks again for taking the time to run through Redwood last week. Quick recap and suggested next steps to keep momentum: 

- We heard that your primary use case is secure, low-latency inference for clinical triage workflows (real-time assistance to nurses).
- Key decision criteria you mentioned: latency <200ms P95 for common prompts, SOC2 + DPA, predictable committed throughput, and clear redline turn times from Legal/Procurement.

Ask / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the internal stakeholders and owners for: economic buyer, security/compliance, legal, and procurement? (I took the liberty of CCing our Legal and Procurement leads for routing support.)
2) If you have an NDA template, please share — otherwise we can send our standard NDA to get that baseline in place.
3) Proposed timeline: provide NDA/contract owners this week -> legal review in 1-2 weeks -> procurement terms and PO by early September (open to faster if your team prefers).

I'll follow up to share our recommended redline sequencing (NDA -> DPA -> MSA) and typical turn times for each team.

Thanks — available for a quick call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182

Laura —

Appreciate the fast follow. I’ve attached our redline-guidance.pdf (sent earlier) and pasted a short sequencing recommendation below to make routing straightforward for your Legal/Procurement: 

Recommended sequencing (minimal friction path):
1) NDA (1-3 business days internal review typical) — get this done first so we can share security artifacts and SOC2 evidence.
2) DPA (privacy terms + data processing specifics) — concurrent review with MSA for any customers requiring HIPAA alignment. Expect 5-10 business days depending on scope.
3) MSA (commercial terms, liability caps, SLAs, indemnities) — procurement/finance negotiation; typical 7-15 business days.

Turn-time notes and owners (Redwood):
- Legal (Neha Kapoor) will own NDA/DPA redlines and initial comments — neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
- Procurement (Priyom Das) will own commercial term discussions and PO sequencing — priyom.das@redwood.ai

Callouts / deal-critical clauses to flag early:
- Liability cap + carve-outs (security incident vs. service performance)
- Data residency/HIPAA handling for PHI (if applicable) — helps determine DPA specifics
- SLA / latency SLOs & remedies (we can propose a latency SLO appendix to the MSA)

Next steps from Redwood: I’ll send our standard NDA to you (unless you prefer we start with yours). Neha — looping you for routing; Priyom — please confirm available review cadence for commercial terms so we can set internal SLAs.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15-min sync with the four of you if useful.

Best,
Marissa
